successors.name: Lordship of Ireland
successors.text: east Ulaid, 'captured and held' at Downpatrick by John de Courcy in 1177

ledger.x: Ulaid before 450: infobox 'Established: Before 450'; 'The Dal Fiatach dynasty held sway over Ulaid until the battle of Leth Cam in 827.'

c. 465: the Cenel nEogain take Inishowen. The Tir Eoghain page (read for tir-eoghain) says 'The territory of Eoghan mac Neill was initially based in Inishowen' and its infobox gives 'c. 465: Eogan mac Neill (first)'; the Ulaid page puts all of Ulster except Cavan in the legendary Ulaid and says the Ulaid 'lost land to…
About 500: the Dal Riata settle in Scotland under Ulaid overlordship.
575: Dal Riata is freed from Ulaid's overlordship.
By the 8th century: 'the territory of the Ulaid shrunk to east of the Bann'.

By the 8th century, as above: the Ulaid page names only 'the Northern Ui Neill' as taker; Donegal beyond Inishowen was the land of the other great Northern Ui Neill branch, the Cenel Conaill, who have no dossier (listed as tir-chonaill).

wars.name: Battle of Moin Dairi Lothair
wars.outcome: The Northern Ui Neill and an alliance of Cruthin kings fought at Moneymore; the Cruthin 'suffered a devastating defeat' and the Airgialla were settled in Eilne.

wars.name: Battle of Moira
wars.outcome: 'the disastrous Battle of Moira in 637, in modern-day County Down, which saw Congal slain.'

wars.name: Norman conquest of Ulaid
wars.outcome: John de Courcy takes Downpatrick in February 1177 and holds it.

certainty.note: The legendary extent, the 450 and 700 shrinkages and the Bann frontier are all approximate.
